title: Pour-Over Coffee Brewed Through a Paper Filter Cone
summary: A precisely controlled brewing method where hot water is poured slowly and evenly over ground coffee, yielding a clean, bright brew.
equipment: pour-over cone (such as a V60) with paper filter

ingredients.item: filtered water (about 150 ml is for rinsing the filter)

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the water to 96–99 °C, just off the boil.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Set the paper filter in the cone, rinse it with about 150 ml hot water to remove the papery taste and warm everything, then discard that water.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the 22 g beans to a medium-fine consistency, like coarse sand.

steps.title: Bloom
steps.text: Put the cone and carafe on the scale, add the coffee, shake level and zero the scale, then start the timer and pour about 50 g water in slow circles to wet all the grounds; let it bloom 30–45 s as it swells.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: Pour in pulses of about 100 g in a pencil-thin stream, circling from the centre outwards and back, letting it drain 10–15 s between pulses but never letting the bed run dry, until the scale reads 350 g.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: If too fast and sour, grind finer; if too slow and bitter, grind coarser; total time should be 3–4 min.

tips: Use a digital scale and timer to dial in the right grind and pouring speed.
A pencil-thin stream of water helps you control the brew and avoid a bitter, overbrewed result.
Each 240 ml serving contains roughly 95 mg of caffeine.
storage: Brew and serve fresh. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
